changes.reason: The description parser re-reads every payment's raw description on first start and stores two more things it found: the bank, and the shape of description it recognised. Every other key a payment had keeps its value.

Sample data seeded by 0.1.2 carried hand-written notes that the raw description does not hold, so on sample payments the note is replaced by what the description says. Payments from a statement keep their note.
The same re-read finds the UPI address and reference in a sample payment's description, which 0.1.2 stored only as a note.
A sample payment whose only stored detail was a hand-written note either has none now (its description holds nothing to read) or gets everything its description holds.

The description parser now reads the first word after the payee in some UPI layouts (UPI/SWIGGY/ORDER/...) as part of the payee key, SWIGGY/ORDER, where 0.1.2 kept SWIGGY. The extra word is a note word and not part of the name, so this is a known rough edge. A key is only ever extended by one word, never replaced.
Migration 027 removes a statement's 'Closing Balance' or 'Opening Balance' label from the end of a payment's description, where an older Kotak reader left it. The planted payment is one such.

Migration 030 clears a merchant name that a machine copied from the bank line (it has two or more slashes), so the payee shows instead. A merchant name you typed, imported or set by your own rule is never touched, which the journey checks with a name typed by hand that has two slashes.
Migration 033 deletes a subcategory that has exactly the same name and parent as another and that nothing uses (no label, rule or policy). The copy that is used, or else the built-in one, stays.

Migration 035 moves 'skipped in Teach Me' from the label to the payment, so a payment with no label can be skipped too. Every payment now carries the field; the skipped ones keep their time, which the snoozedAt comparison checks.
Migration 036 fills the category id that 0.1.2's sample-data seeder left empty, only where the name matches exactly one category, and checks that the id names the label. A filled id is never changed.
Migration 036, for the subcategory id.
Migration 030, as stored: the label's own merchant column, where a machine copied the bank line. The invariant on every label column holds the labels you made by hand to no change at all.
0.1.2 has no review policies to read. The upgraded ledger has none either, because nobody created one.
0.1.2 has no taxonomy tidy-up report. The upgraded ledger has no duplicate and no orphaned categories, which is what migrations 033 and 036 are for.
Learned merchant rules are kept per direction (money out or in) since migration 029.

Teach Me now holds every payment with no category, including payments with no label at all and machine labels of Uncategorized at any confidence. The journey checks that each payment it newly holds had no category before.
The queue counts endpoint is new: 0.1.2 only reported how many were set aside, which is unchanged.
The settings payload says whether an AI provider is switched on, so the app can word its messages for a setup with no model. The journey runs with none.

The Dashboard headline said 'kept' for what was invested plus what was kept. Kept is now In - Out - Invested everywhere: headline, tile and Money Map, and the headline says what was invested. The journey checks the new headline equals the Kept figure.
The first month has no month before it. It used to compare against zeros and now shows no comparison and no delta.
'What changed' lists nothing for the first month, which has no month to compare with. It used to list every category against zero.
A month still running is compared with the same days of the previous month, not with all of it. Optional because on the last day of a month nothing is partial.
The same like-for-like comparison, for the categories that moved: a category the same days of the previous month did not hold is left out, and one that held money then and none now appears.

Where it went now ends with reconciling lines (Transfers and cash, and Refunds and paybacks taken off the rows above) so the rows add up to Out. The category rows themselves are unchanged. The journey checks that the rows and the lines add up to Out.

The Dashboard's 'Spoken for each month' added every active recurring charge, whatever its cadence, and so disagreed with Money Map. Both now show the monthly charges that are still running. The journey checks it equals Money Map's header.
The people panel shows the month it sits on. It used to show all time under every month, so a person with no payments in a month is no longer listed there.
The same: a person's sent, received, net and count are the month's. The journey checks that a person's months add up to the all-time figure the panel used to show.
One definition of unsorted everywhere: a payment with no label counts, as well as one labelled Uncategorized. The journey checks the figure never shrinks.

A statement says how many of its payments are sorted, counted the way Teach Me counts: a payment is sorted when it has a real category and is not a machine guess below your confidence bar. It replaces the old annotated count, which counted every payment the machine had labelled, however unsure. The journey checks each figure against the payments themselves.
Replaced by the sorted count. The journey checks that the old figure was the number of labelled payments, and that no statement has more sorted payments than it had labelled ones.

The statement list no longer reports how many payments have a vector in the AI memory, because that is a machine detail and not something to act on. It was 0 here: the journey runs with no embedding model.

A payment can now carry a name you gave it (display_name), and its payee a name you gave the payee (payee_name). The journey renames nothing, so both are empty, and so is the cleaned-up note, which no sample or fixture payment has.
A payment can now carry a note you wrote on it (user_note). The journey writes none, so every payment starts with none.
Each payment now says whether the note it shows is one you wrote. None is, because you wrote none.

Every payment now says what it is called (payee, and payee_all for the payee as a whole), and by which channel it was made (UPI, NEFT, Card...). A group member carries the same fields as its payment. These are read off what is stored and change nothing in it. The journey checks that a payment reads as its merchant, or else as the payee exactly as the bank printed it, and that a group member agrees with its payment.
A learned rule in Settings > Rules shows the name of its payee. The journey checks it is the name that payee goes by on its payments.
Migration 037 adds the table that holds the names you give to payees. It starts empty.
Migration 038 adds the table that lets Teach Me undo an answer. It starts empty.
Migration 037 adds the column that holds the name you give to a single payment. Every payment starts with none.
Migration 042 adds the column that holds the note you write on a payment. Every payment starts with none.
Migration 039 lets a waiting sorting job remember which payments it covers. Jobs that already ran have no scope.
Migration 040 counts how many times a sorting job has been started.
A sorting job that finished before the upgrade starts with an attempt count of 0, and the upgrade starts none.
Migration 027 strips a trailing balance label from descriptions. It runs once, on the first start of the new release.
Migration 028 records which text each AI-memory vector was built from. It runs once, on the first start of the new release.
Migration 029 keeps dismissed learned rules per payee and direction. It runs once, on the first start of the new release.
Migration 030 clears merchant names a machine copied from the bank line. It runs once, on the first start of the new release.
Migration 031 adds review policies. It runs once, on the first start of the new release.
Migration 032 lets a label made by a review policy carry its own source. It runs once, on the first start of the new release.
Migration 033 deletes an unused duplicate subcategory. It runs once, on the first start of the new release.
Migration 034 adds the tidy-up suggestions you dismissed. It runs once, on the first start of the new release.
Migration 035 moves "skipped in Teach Me" from the label to the payment. It runs once, on the first start of the new release.
Migration 036 fills category ids the old sample-data seeder left empty. It runs once, on the first start of the new release.
Migration 037 adds payee and payment names. It runs once, on the first start of the new release.
Migration 038 adds the records that let Teach Me undo an answer. It runs once, on the first start of the new release.
Migration 039 lets a waiting sorting job remember its payments. It runs once, on the first start of the new release.
Migration 040 counts how many times a sorting job has been started. It runs once, on the first start of the new release.
Migration 042 adds notes on payments. It runs once, on the first start of the new release.

A recurring charge to a payee with no merchant name is listed under the payee as the bank printed it, instead of the printed name in title case, so Recurring, Money Map and the Ledger call it the same thing.
The same row under its new name. Its amount, cadence and category are unchanged, which the journey checks for every recurring row: a name may change in case and nothing else.

The same change as the two entries before it, seen from the other side: a recurring row is keyed by its category when its newest charge has one, and by its name when it has none. Which one the journey meets depends on the day it runs (whether the newest charge of the demo data has been sorted by then), so each shape has an entry and none is required; the journey's own check holds that a name changes in case and nothing else.

Every statement now belongs to an account, found by the bank and the account number printed on the statement, and carries the account's name as the app words it (the bank and the last four digits until you name it, or the words you typed in the old Rename).
The period a statement prints in its header is kept beside the dates of its first and last payment. Statements added before it existed have none, and the upgrade does not guess one: it starts empty.

The statement list no longer carries the whole account number, only its last four digits. The number stays in the ledger as the account's key. These are the two uploaded sample statements, which print XXXX0000.
The same, for the sample statements, which print no number.
The last four digits of the account number replace the whole number in the statement list. The journey checks each is the last four of the number it had.
The same, for the sample statements, which have no number to shorten.
0.1.2 has no accounts to read. The upgraded ledger has one account for each bank (and each account number a bank printed), made from its existing statements, with no name until you give one.
Migration 041 adds the table that holds your accounts and fills it from the statements you already have.
Migration 041 gives each statement the account it belongs to and the period it prints.
Migration 041 adds accounts. It runs once, on the first start of the new release.

A statement now records how many payments its file held and how many of them were new, because a statement that overlaps an earlier one adds only the new ones. Every statement you already had brought all the payments of its file, so both are its payment count, which the journey checks.

The running-balance check of a statement's whole file is now stored with it, so a statement whose overlapping rows were skipped never looks unbalanced. For every statement you already had it is the check the list showed before: the journey checks the stored figures equal that check and that nothing that was balanced is flagged now.

The statement list says on which days and in which months a statement's own payments fall, because a statement can cover days in a month it brought no payment for. They are worked out from the payments, which the journey checks.

The statement list says how many of a statement's payments another statement of the account also had and did not add again, so deleting it can say they are removed from the ledger for good. No statement you already had skipped payments, so every statement starts at 0.
Migration 043 gives each statement what its file held, what of it was new, and the balance check of the file.
Migration 043 records what each statement's file held and whether its balance checked out. It runs once, on the first start of the new release.

A payment now says when it is paired with a payment in another of your accounts as a transfer (Moved to ..., Moved from ...). Pairing runs when a statement is added, never on upgrade, so every payment starts unpaired.

A payment now says when its Transfers guess is held back because it could be a move between your own accounts. It is read off the labels and the other payments, changes nothing stored, and no payment of the journey's ledger is held back.
Migration 044 adds the table that remembers the transfers you took apart, so they are not paired again. It starts empty.

Migration 044 lets a label come from a pair of statements and adds the table of unpaired transfers. It rebuilds the table that holds labels with every label, source, confidence and note as it was, and it runs once, on the first start of the new release.
